newsitem.title: UK: England keeper Banks says Grobbelaar no match fixer.
newsitem.headline: England keeper Banks says Grobbelaar no match fixer.

text.p: Gordon Banks, one of England's greatest goalkeepers, said on Wednesday he could find no evidence that Bruce Grobbelaar let goals in deliberately.
Banks, asked to study five matches at the centre of match-fixing allegations, said Grobbelaar's performance ranged from good to excellent.

Banks, goalkeeper in England's 1966 World Cup victory, told a court in the southern city of Winchester that there was not a scrap of evidence to suggest Grobbelaar acted improperly or tried to engineer Liverpool's defeat.

Grobbelaar is accused with former Wimbledon goalkeeper Hans Segers, ex-Wimbledon and Aston Villa striker John Fashanu and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim of rigging games to benefit an Asian betting syndicate.
All four defendants deny the charges although both keepers admit they were paid in cash by Lim for providing match forecasts.

The jury has heard that in a secretly filmed conversation with his former business associate Chris Vincent, Grobbelaar said he had lost 125,000 pounds ($202,000) when he instinctively made two "blinding saves" in Liverpool's 3-3 draw against Manchester United in January 1994.
Banks, asked about two saves by Grobbelaar in that match, told the court: "Apparently he was alleged to have been diving the wrong way.
"In my opinion, I must have been keeping goal the wrong way all the years I played because I would have made a lot more saves if I had been diving the wrong way."
As defence lawyers wrapped up their case in this southern English town, former Liverpool defender Alan Hansen said Grobbelaar was flamboyant and arrogant.

But Hansen, now a soccer pundit on television, told the court: "I wouldn't call him a good goalkeeper. I would call him a great goalkeeper. You don't win as many medals and play as many games for Liverpool as he did without being one."
Hansen said Grobbelaar was as committed as any other player in the team.
"It would never have entered my head that any player in that team (that) was winning everything in sight would have anything less than 100 percent commitment to the cause," he told the court.
During a 13-year career with Liverpool, Grobbelaar won five league championships and one European Cup. He is English soccer's most successful club goalkeeper. ($ = 0.618 British Pounds)
